Michael / Marissa — attaching the first draft of the annotated flow (redwood_dataflow_edge_v2.png). Notes inline: 

- Inference request path: client -> regional edge proxy -> regional inference pool -> (optional) cross-region fallback pool. Only request metadata and aggregated latency metrics leave the region by default; full request payloads are routed only when the customer has region-exempted deployment.
- KV cache note: caches are per-region and TTL-based. When caching is enabled for throughput-sensitive routes, cached KV entries do not persist PII beyond the configured TTL and are encrypted at rest with customer-specific KMS keys for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Telemetry & logs: token-level logs are considered operational artifacts and are only accessible to ops SREs for debugging under an audited workflow; access requires approval and is logged. Subprocessors (e.g., cloud provider managed logging) may host aggregated telemetry but do not receive token-level payloads unless explicitly enabled in the contract.
- Egress paths: diagram shows two egress lanes — (1) telemetry aggregation lane to the analytics region (pseudonymized when sent), (2) emergency fallback lane for model failover (encrypted).

I left a placeholder for retention durations — Marissa, suggest we commit to 30 days for raw logs by default and 13 months for aggregated telemetry unless the customer requests stricter retention. Happy to change based on compliance ask.

Folks — see my answers below (I also uploaded a short DPA notes doc to the drive — DPA_draft_notes.docx).

- PI/PHI classification: 
  * Patient identifiers (names, DOB, patient_id, contact info) — PII/PHI.
  * Hashed patient IDs — treated as pseudonymized identifiers; for Clarity's DPA we should treat these as PII unless they are explicitly salted and stored outside the inference path.
  * Clinical text (notes, diagnoses) — may contain PHI; we recommend that customers opt into in-pipeline redaction or use private deployments for sensitive workloads.

- Subprocessor access to token-level logs:
  * By default, token-level logs are retained in-region for 30 days and are accessible only to Engineering SREs (audited) and a limited set of Troubleshooting engineers under a documented access request.
  * Subprocessors (cloud-managed logging, analytics pipelines) receive only aggregated telemetry unless the customer signs an explicit subprocessor access appendix granting them token access.

- Retention recommendations:
  * Raw token logs: 30 days default, max 90 days with justification.
  * Aggregated telemetry/metrics: 13 months default for product analytics.
  * Pseudonymization: ensure hashed IDs are salted per-customer where possible and provide salted-hash proofs for audits.

I also recommend adding a clause in the processing annex that requires Clarity to provide documented justification for any retention > 90 days.
